title: Recuerdos
subtitle: Childhood & how things used to be

lessons.title: When I was little
lessons.goal: Describe where you lived and what life was like as a child.

tip.title: era, tenía, vivía: the imperfect
tip.body: To describe how things used to be, Spanish uses the imperfect (pretérito imperfecto). -ar verbs take -aba: jugar → jugaba. -er and -ir verbs take -ía: tener → tenía, vivir → vivía. The "I" and "he/she" forms are the same, so add a name or pronoun when it isn't clear. Start a memory with cuando era pequeño (a man) / pequeña (a woman), or, for everyone, cuando tenía diez años or en mi infancia.

lessons.title: Games & habits
lessons.goal: Say what you used to do as a child.

tip.title: Habits in the past
tip.body: The imperfect also describes habits: things you did again and again, like English "used to" or "would". Words like siempre, todos los días, a menudo (often) and los veranos go well with it. Childhood words vary by region: cartoons are dibujos animados in Spain and caricaturas in Mexico; hide-and-seek is el escondite in Spain and las escondidas in Mexico; to ride a bike is montar en bici in Spain and andar en bici in Mexico.

lessons.title: Calling an old friend
lessons.goal: Call an old friend, share a memory and suggest meeting up.

tip.title: ¿Te acuerdas?
tip.body: In Spain people answer the phone with ¿Sí? or ¿Dígame?; in Mexico you'll hear ¿Bueno?. To talk about remembering, use acordarse de: ¿Te acuerdas de mí? Claro que me acuerdo. Add a shared memory with ¿Te acuerdas de cuando …? plus the imperfect: ¿Te acuerdas de cuando íbamos al río? ¡Cuánto tiempo! means "It's been ages!". In Spain quedar means to meet up (¿Quedamos mañana?); in Mexico people say ¿Nos vemos mañana?

It's been ages!

Of course I remember!
It's so good to hear from you!
What have you been up to?

lessons.title: Imperfect or indefinido?
lessons.goal: Use the imperfect for habits and background, the indefinido for single events.

tip.title: Background vs. event
tip.body: Spanish has two main past tenses. The imperfect (jugaba, tenía, vivía) sets the scene: descriptions, background and habits, like English "used to" or "was …ing". Only three verbs are irregular: ser → era, ir → iba, ver → veía. The indefinido (jugué, tuve, fui) tells single, finished events, often with un día, ayer or el verano pasado. Together: Jugábamos en el parque (background) cuando empezó a llover (event). Adjectives still agree: cuando era pequeño (man), cuando era pequeña (woman).

lessons.title: Grandpa's village
lessons.goal: Follow a grandfather's memories of village life.

phrases.n: What was the village like before?
We didn't have a TV.

phrases.t: Nos sentábamos en la puerta a tomar el fresco.
phrases.n: We used to sit by the front door to enjoy the cool evening air.
phrases.note: tomar el fresco: to sit outside when the evening cools down, a summer custom in Spanish villages.

phrases.t: Conocí a tu abuela en las fiestas del pueblo.
phrases.n: I met your grandmother at the village festival.

story.title: Abuelo Antonio
story.intro: Paula asks her grandfather Antonio what life was like in his village in Castile when he was a child.

lines.name: Paula
lines.t: Abuelo, ¿cómo era el pueblo cuando eras pequeño?
lines.n: Grandpa, what was the village like when you were little?

lines.name: Antonio
lines.t: Era muy diferente. Vivían muchas más familias y había niños por todas partes.
lines.n: It was very different. Many more families lived there and there were children everywhere.

lines.name: Paula
lines.t: ¿Y teníais tele?
lines.n: And did you have a TV?

lines.name: Antonio
lines.t: No, no teníamos tele. Jugábamos en la calle todo el día, y por las noches nos sentábamos en la puerta a tomar el fresco con los vecinos.
lines.n: No, we didn't have a TV. We played in the street all day, and in the evenings we sat by the door enjoying the cool air with the neighbours.

lines.name: Paula
lines.t: ¿Ibas al colegio en el pueblo?
lines.n: Did you go to school in the village?

lines.name: Antonio
lines.t: Sí, había una escuela pequeña con una sola maestra para todos los niños.
lines.n: Yes, there was a small school with just one teacher for all the children.

lines.name: Paula
lines.t: ¿Y en verano?
lines.n: And in summer?

lines.name: Antonio
lines.t: En verano ayudaba a mi padre en el campo. Y un verano conocí a tu abuela en las fiestas del pueblo.
lines.n: In summer I helped my father in the fields. And one summer I met your grandmother at the village festival.

lessons.title: My childhood
lessons.goal: Talk about your childhood for 60 seconds.

culture.title: Summers in the pueblo
culture.body: Many families in Spain have roots in a small village, which they simply call el pueblo, because parents or grandparents moved to the cities in the second half of the 20th century. For many Spaniards, childhood memories mean long summer holidays there with grandparents and cousins: playing in the street until late, riding bikes and going to the village fiestas, which in many places are held in summer. In Mexico, classic childhood games include canicas (marbles), el trompo (the spinning top) and la lotería, a bingo-like game with picture cards that many families still play at get-togethers. Ask a Spanish speaker ¿A qué jugabas de pequeño? and you may well get a long, happy answer.

phrases.t: Pasaba los veranos en el pueblo.
phrases.n: I used to spend the summers in the village.

phrases.t: Jugábamos a la lotería con mis abuelos.
phrases.n: We used to play lotería with my grandparents.
It was a very happy time.
I miss those summers.
phrases.note: Mexico and much of Latin America: extraño aquellos veranos.

free.n: Talk about your childhood: where you lived, what your home was like, who was important to you, what you used to do and one special memory.
free.hint: Use Cuando era pequeño/a … / Cuando tenía … años, vivía en …, Vivíamos en una casa …, Todos los días jugaba …, Los veranos íbamos …, Un día / Un verano …, Era una época ….
free.model: Cuando era pequeño, vivía en un pueblo cerca del mar. Vivíamos en una casa vieja con un jardín grande. Todos los días jugaba en la calle con mis primos, y los veranos íbamos a la playa con mis abuelos. Mi abuela nos contaba cuentos por la noche. Un verano aprendí a nadar y fui al mar todos los días. Era una época muy feliz.

prompts.n: Say it was a very happy time.

lessons.title: A2 speaking test
lessons.goal: Pass to earn your A2 badge and unlock B1.

tip.title: You can do this
tip.body: The test mixes phrases from all the A2 units: what you did recently, travel, health, your home, work, plans for the future, restaurants and childhood memories. Answer in full sentences, take a breath before you speak, and don't worry about small mistakes: being understood is what counts.
